instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: No Tie Stands
cards.instruction: Turn every even outcome into a formal rematch with a new rule and a consequence for losing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our cakes tied. Blindfolded icing next; loser cleans the kitchen. You learnt to hold that piping bag from me, so let's see what stuck.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A tie is a perfectly good result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can match your teacher now. Lovely. You still have to beat me; put the blindfold by your bowl.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't want another cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we use these two cakes. One hand behind your back, neatest icing wins; loser cleans up. I showed you how to pipe one-handed. Let's see if you can do it without me guiding you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've paid exactly the same. One tiebreaker: describe dinner without saying 'nice'; loser pays the tip. Remember the table manners I taught you?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why should anyone lose?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can split a bill without my help now. Let's see if you can finish a sentence without 'nice'. Your turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We both enjoyed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Another tie. New rule: one adjective each, no repeats; first repeat pays the tip. Like our restaurant practice, only this time you can beat me. I choose 'crispy'.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Every Loss Builds the Comeback
cards.instruction: Treat each setback as proof that the eventual victory will be more impressive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Six losses will make our first win glorious. Get the team together; I taught you how to give a captain's talk when nobody wanted to listen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The tournament is over.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're checking the calendar now. Good. Next season they'll see us come back from six straight defeats. Call the players.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Our team is disbanding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then winning after a reunion will be even better. Start with one player, like I showed you when you first became captain. Tell them I want their name on that comeback team.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My collapsed cake will make the winning one look enormous. Get the bowl; I taught you how to start again without staring at the wreckage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You've burned the oven out.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You found the fault before mixing; progress. Winning with a replacement oven will be better still. Ring the appliance shop.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The competition's tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ask for delivery tonight. Winning after that will shut up everyone who saw this cake. Use the firm voice we practised: an oven tonight, not next week.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Congratulate Through Your Teeth
cards.instruction: Perform warm praise while allowing competitive resentment to intensify beneath every compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Congratulations on beating my poem. Lovely to see the rhythm I taught you carrying so much of it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Are you saying I didn't deserve the prize?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No, you've come miles since I counted every beat for you. The judges even enjoyed that last line I asked you to change.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That isn't much of a compliment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A wonderful first prize for my pupil. When you read it out, thank me for those rhythm lessons. Give my name the same care you gave that last line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful promotion. I trained you to write those reports, and now you get the director's office I applied for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I worked for this.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. You stopped sending me your drafts eventually. Beautiful timing, too, having one ready just when the director retired.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't you just be happy for me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Delighted. Your first report as director will be a pleasure to correct. Send it to me before the board; I'll try not to leave the page quite so red this time.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Nothing Without Stakes
cards.instruction: Price every request and decision with a reward, penalty, bargain, or trade.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Borrow my ladder if I get first choice at your barbecue. I taught you to ask what a job pays before carrying the tools.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can't it just be a favour?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good word; you used to call it free labour. What are you offering for this favour?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Friendship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then show me the friend's portion. Put two sausages aside and I'll bring the ladder. Be specific, like I taught you: two with my name on them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: If I apologise first, what do I get? I taught you to put an offer on the table before asking for a concession.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: An end to this argument.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better; you used to offer silence and call it peace. Does your apology come with that, or only mine?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's not a game.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we can drop the winning and keep the trade. I'll say I was wrong to shout if you say I was right about the bill. Two sentences, like we practised.

cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Fair Means I Can Win
cards.instruction: Agree to any rule or bargain only after interpreting fairness in a way that preserves your advantage.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll race if I get a head start. I carried the hurdles up the stairs; I taught you to count fatigue when setting a handicap.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We've all had a tiring morning.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You remembered the other runners this time. Good. Now count my stairs as well. Put my start two paces ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We start on the same line.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Agreed, once you bend my bit forward. You used to need me to draw the handicap marks; show me you can give your old coach a fair start.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll agree to equal slices once mine includes the baking time. Remember how I taught you to cost a cake, not just weigh it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That gives you a bigger slice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've noticed the difference; good. Now add the hours I spent teaching you to get the middle cooked. Cut mine on that line.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ate the spare icing already.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That was testing the consistency. Keep tasting separate from portions, the way I showed you. Then we can call these shares equal and you can hand me mine.
